How to Extract JSON Path: Developer Guide & Technical Reference

The fastest way to extract JSON path queries, evaluate complex filters, and inspect hierarchical structures directly in your browser.

What is JSONPath?

When you need to extract JSON path expressions from complex, nested payloads, JSONPath provides a standardized declarative query language. Similar to what XPath delivers for XML, JSONPath gives developers and data engineers a straightforward syntax to navigate hierarchical documents, isolate targeted nodes, filter elements within arrays, and extract exact data points without writing manual traversal loops.

From inspecting microservice payloads and debugging REST API responses to automating end-to-end integration tests, this tool lets you extract JSON path values and validate query results with zero latency.

JSONPath Syntax Cheat Sheet

Compare standard JSONPath operators, recursive descent notations, wildcards, and filter expressions in the reference table below:

Common JSONPath Operators and Expressions
Operator Name Description Example Expression
$ Root Object Represents the root object or array from which all JSONPath expressions originate. $ or $.store.book
@ Current Node Refers to the current element being processed in a filter predicate or array iterator. [?(@.price < 20)]
.. Recursive Descent Deep scan selector that traverses recursively across all child and descendant levels to find matching keys. $..author or $..id
[*] Array Wildcard Matches all elements contained in an array, or all property values within an object. $.store.book[*]
[?()] Filter Expression Applies a logical boolean expression to filter items within an array or collection. $.data[?(@.type == 'articles')]
* Wildcard Matches any property name or value at the current hierarchical level. $.store.*
['key'] Bracket Notation Selects a property by string key; essential for keys containing spaces, hyphens, or special characters. $['store']['book name']
[start:end:step] Array Slice Extracts a slice of array elements using start, end, and optional step indices. $.books[0:2]

Frequently Asked Questions

What is JSONPath?

JSONPath is an expression language for querying and extracting specific elements, properties, and values from JSON documents. Similar to XPath for XML, JSONPath provides a standardized syntax to traverse tree-like data structures, filter array items, and extract targeted data without manual traversal.

Is this JSONPath evaluator secure?

Yes, completely. This JSONPath extractor operates 100% client-side directly within your web browser. None of your JSON data, payloads, or query expressions are ever uploaded, transmitted, or logged on remote servers. All parsing, path synthesis, and evaluation occur locally on your machine.
